Goals.Goal: **(1) A refused supersede leaves no successor minted by that invocation, except where the bounded cleanup policy must preserve bytes.** With or without `--replacement`, every refusal class — validation before any write, a fold the stream cannot satisfy, an existing minted candidate, an archive-destination conflict, a missing or archived predecessor or `spec.xml`, an invalid replacement relation or status, and the post-fold governance/rename/cleanup failures below — leaves `.ngrace/changes/active/` without any directory this invocation created, **or** leaves that directory plus an explicit residual-state diagnostic naming it and the reason cleanup was refused. A refusal never silently orphans a successor, and never deletes, moves, or rewrites a directory that already existed before the invocation (explicit `--replacement` target, a pre-existing candidate, or a competitor's directory). **Preservation boundary, exact:** identity/content differences visible at validation, foreign names visible at enumeration, and `rmdir` `ENOTEMPTY` are handled by CL-2; cooperating writers serialize on the lock; a non-cooperating writer that replaces this invocation's own file **after** byte validation but **before** unlink is outside the supported model and is not claimed safe; SIGKILL/power loss remains the separate uncatchable interruption window. Repeating a refusal against the **same still-active predecessor** has exact outcomes: under a **cleaned** refusal the active-set count is unchanged; under a **retained-residue** refusal the named directory remains and a repeat with the **same resolved candidate id** refuses at acquisition (the id exists) so no second directory is added, while a repeat with a **new timestamp** resolves a new id and may itself be retained-and-named. The criterion asserts those exact outcomes and does not promise a globally constant count under new-timestamp retries. The policy is stated consistently in the taxonomy, in the bounded-cleanup and synchronization Constraints, and in `AC-CLEANUP-BOUNDED`.

**(2) Mint ownership is exclusive at acquisition and bounded at cleanup.** `ngrace spec new` and the implicit mint inside `ngrace supersede` acquire their candidate directory atomically: losing a race between the existence check and creation is a refusal that writes nothing, not an overwrite. A competing `spec.xml` created after the check is preserved; a competitor's unrelated file in the same directory is preserved; a freshly minted `spec.xml` is created exclusively, never truncating an existing one. **Exclusive acquisition does not prove continuing ownership:** a competitor can write into an acquired directory after the ownership scan, and a scan-then-delete is itself racy. Cleanup therefore removes a directory only when this invocation created it **and** it holds no artifact this invocation did not write at the moment of removal; if removal fails, or a foreign artifact appears (including one written by a competitor after the ownership check), the invocation refuses, preserves the residue, and emits a diagnostic naming the directory and the reason. Cleanup's preservation promise is bounded to what validation can observe: identity mismatch, changed own bytes, foreign entries, and `rmdir` `ENOTEMPTY` are refused and preserved; a non-cooperating replacement between the byte comparison and the unlink is outside the supported model and is not claimed safe. The C-HASHED-BUNDLE-IDS-2 promise "refusal writes nothing — no directory, no file" is preserved for acquisition and narrowed for cleanup exactly as this bounded contract states.

**(3) Every success path keeps its established shape.** A successful supersede retains the lineage successor, the predecessor's `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` root status set to `superseded` with a `<Replacement>` naming the successor, the open epoch folded, the predecessor moved to `archive/`, source bytes unchanged, and stdout exactly the archive-relative path. Corrected from this draft's earlier claim: successful folding **deletes the verified loose files but leaves the `run/` directory in place**, possibly empty — measured on the authority fixture (`runExists: true`, `runFiles: []`). Ledger payload equivalence is stated through the canonical projection `expectedLedgerEventAttributes` (which strips `graceVersion` and normalizes `id`/`task`/`kind`) plus children — never through raw attribute equality, and never by feeding the verifier the writer's own `eventAttributesForLedger` output. Spec-only bundles (no `plan.xml`, no `run/`) keep superseding with exit 0.

**(4) Interrupted folding recovers against the durable ledger, as the shipped contract requires.** [C-RUN-LEDGER](.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RUN-LEDGER/spec.xml)'s `AC-FOLD-ORDERING` states: *"a failure injected between write and delete leaves both the ledger and the loose files, and a follow-up fold is idempotent rather than duplicating the epoch."* That contract is violated at both shipped fault hooks today: the retry advances the epoch number and appends a second epoch carrying the same events. The repair compares the loose event set to the durable ledger **before** loose-only closure/hole checks or synthesized auto-open can misclassify the residue, and distinguishes three cases: (i) a loose event whose id **and** canonical payload match an event in the last recorded epoch is already-recorded residue and is not re-added; when the whole loose set is such residue — the state after an interruption, including a **partial deletion of the verified prefix** — the retry reuses that epoch number, deletes the remaining loose files, and writes no new epoch and no synthesized `opened`; (ii) a loose event whose id matches **no** recorded event was newly allocated after the interruption and folds into the next epoch under the normal allocator; (iii) a loose event whose id matches a recorded event but whose canonical payload differs is a genuine conflict and is refused without writes. Repeated interruptions remain idempotent; each event appears exactly once under the epoch that owns it; payload preservation is asserted independently. The **mixed set** — recorded residue plus normally allocated fresh events — is ordered so its refusal promise is satisfiable: **all** residue/conflict checks and **all** fresh-event foldability checks run **before any destructive action**, so an invalid-fresh refusal deletes nothing and materializes no auto-open; only then is the already-recorded residue deleted, the fresh set's legitimate auto-open materialized, the new epoch written, and the fresh loose files deleted. Auto-open is materialized only after validation passes, so it is never written on a **pre-mutation validation refusal** (an **injected interruption after stage (ii-c)** preserves the **F ∪ A** it already made), and the old residue is deleted before the new ledger write so a later retry cannot see it as an older-epoch overlap (`AC-FOLD-MIXED-RECOVERY`). Ownership is by the **interrupted logical fold and its verified evidence**, not by process identity: a later CLI invocation may perform the recovery.

**(5) Disappearing entries are tolerated; unparseable existing entries are refused at fold.** In both measured windows of F295 (a file removed after `readdirSync` before the callee existence check; a file removed after that check before the read), the reader omits the vanished entry and `ngrace cursor show` exits 0. The consequence is **not** a universal fold refusal: an interior hole refuses (`range hole at N for w0`), while a trailing event with a closer still present folds, and a vanished `opened` event is covered by the deliberate single-controller auto-open of D8.2 (`ngrace cursor fold` exit 0, a covering `opened` synthesized). A malformed `<broken` loose file is **not** a disappearance and must not become false evidence: the read-only inventory may keep its filename fallback (`cursor show` exits 0), and lint deliberately does **not** validate loose `run/` XML (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1569`; the division is [C-RUN-LEDGER](.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RUN-LEDGER/spec.xml:124-126)), but the **authoritative folding boundary refuses** an existing-but-unparseable loose file (reader `xml.parse`, `root: null`) **before** any `discarded` write, auto-open, or ledger write, naming the file and the parse error and preserving every input byte. `EISDIR`/`EACCES` remain discriminating refusals. The parallel `listRunOrphans` is covered by a direct assertion and a real consuming CLI path.

**(6) The discarded preflight is bounded honestly and the allocator is untouched.** The unnecessary engine-authored `discarded` residue is removed for a stream that is already deterministically unfoldable **at the snapshot the preflight reads**. The preflight cannot promise the later `foldEpoch` will never refuse — a competing writer can change the stream after the snapshot. **Selected contract: retain the bounded direct seam as an explicit non-cooperating robustness case; no plan-time serialization alternative remains.** Supported neo-grace writers are serialized by the candidate lock, and the test callback runs inside that lock and models a controlled **non-cooperating filesystem actor** outside the supported-writer population; its guarantee is deliberately narrow: if that actor changes the stream after preflight, the fold refuses with the stage-(ii-a) `discarded` residue preserved, and after that same actor reverses only its own mutation a real fold consumes the residue exactly once (`AC-DISCARD-NOT-WRITTEN-ON-PREWRITE-REFUSE`). This does not expand CL-2 to arbitrary non-cooperating candidate-file replacement and does not call the callback a cooperating public writer. The existing per-bundle `.run-write.lock`, the post-write uniqueness scan, the own-file unlink/retry, and the single-controller auto-open rule are preserved unchanged, and the preflight mirrors fold's allocation semantics rather than inventing a stricter one.

**(7) The paid F158 defect is closed; the two bounded residue boundaries are preserved, not promised away.** F158's exact measured reproduction — a **too-narrow allocation** (an event outside every allocation, `unterminated range`) that still appended an engine-authored `discarded` event before the ledger error — is **eliminated**: the pre-flight refusal now runs before `discarded` is written, so that reproduction adds no `run/` file, leaves the ledger byte-identical, and leaves no invocation-created successor (`AC-F158-DEFECT-CLOSED`). Both bounded residues are explicitly recorded and never deleted by a refuse path. No criterion claims full transactionality, no criterion forbids the evidence either bounded boundary necessarily produces, and no criterion relabels the post-ledger boundary as F158.

An executable close-time discriminator covers both tracked and untracked changes against the named base commit, with a closed allowed-write set, and is proved by a planted forbidden write on a disposable fixture. The ignored `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` input is a **transient pre-flush mutation** declared by digest outside the guard's observable population; it is not a guard-observed write.

(2) **Continuing ownership** — not assumed: a competitor can write into an acquired directory after any ownership scan.
